title: Tattvabodha
subtitle: A prose primer on Vedānta · traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara

source.edition: The Ātmabodha, with its Commentary; also the Tattwa-bodha, Orphan School Press, Mirzapore, 1852; recensional readings vary.
source.digitalText: Original English translation and word-for-word gloss prepared for this reader.
source.note: Traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara. Some manuscript colophons credit Vāsudevendra; the text and its section divisions vary between editions.

translationCredit: Original English translation and word-for-word gloss prepared for this reader.

units.label: Opening invocation
units.deva:
वासुदेवेन्द्रयोगीन्द्रं नत्वा ज्ञानप्रदं गुरुम् ।
मुमुक्षूणां हितार्थाय तत्त्वबोधोऽभिधीयते ॥
units.translation: Having bowed to Vāsudevendra, foremost among yogis and the guru who bestows knowledge, this teaching on reality is set forth for the benefit of seekers of liberation.

units.label: Purpose of the teaching
units.deva: साधनचतुष्टयसम्पन्नाधिकारिणां मोक्षसाधनभूतं तत्त्वविवेकप्रकारं वक्ष्यामः ।
units.translation: We shall explain the method of discerning reality, which is a means to liberation, for qualified students endowed with the fourfold preparation.

gloss.en: serving as a means to liberation

units.label: The four preparations
units.deva:
साधनचतुष्टयं किम् ?
नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः ।
इहामुत्रार्थफलभोगविरागः ।
शमादिषट्कसम्पत्तिः ।
मुमुक्षुत्वं चेति ।
units.translation: What are the four preparations? Discernment between the permanent and impermanent; dispassion toward enjoying the fruits of action here and hereafter; the sixfold discipline beginning with śama; and the desire for liberation.

gloss.en: dispassion toward enjoying the fruits of action
the six disciplines beginning with śama

units.label: Discernment
units.deva:
नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः कः ?
नित्यवस्त्वेकं ब्रह्म तद्व्यतिरिक्तं सर्वमनित्यम् ।
अयमेव नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः ।
units.translation: What is discernment between the permanent and impermanent? Brahman alone is permanent; everything apart from it is impermanent. This alone is such discernment.

units.label: Dispassion
units.deva:
विरागः कः ?
इहस्वर्गभोगेषु इच्छाराहित्यम् ।
units.translation: What is dispassion? It is freedom from desire for enjoyments in this world and in heaven.

units.label: The sixfold discipline
units.deva:
शमादिसाधनसम्पत्तिः का ?
शमो दम उपरमस्तितिक्षा श्रद्धा समाधानं च इति ।
units.translation: What is the group of disciplines beginning with śama? They are śama, dama, uparama, titikṣā, śraddhā, and samādhāna.

units.label: Śama — calm of mind
units.deva:
शमः कः ?
मनोनिग्रहः ।
units.translation: What is śama? Restraint of the mind.

units.label: Dama — restraint of the senses
units.deva:
दमः कः ?
चक्षुरादिबाह्येन्द्रियनिग्रहः ।
units.translation: What is dama? Restraint of the external senses, beginning with sight.

units.label: Uparama — steady conduct
units.deva:
उपरमः कः ?
स्वधर्मानुष्ठानमेव ।
units.translation: What is uparama? Steady observance of one’s own duty.

units.label: Titikṣā — forbearance
units.deva:
तितिक्षा का ?
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखादिसहिष्णुत्वम् ।
units.translation: What is forbearance? The capacity to endure cold and heat, pleasure and pain, and the like.

units.label: Śraddhā — trust in the teaching
units.deva:
श्रद्धा कीदृशी ?
गुरुवेदान्तवाक्यादिषु विश्वासः श्रद्धा ।
units.translation: What is the nature of śraddhā? Trust in the teacher, the statements of Vedānta, and the like is śraddhā.

gloss.en: in Vedānta statements and the like

units.label: Samādhāna — collected attention
units.deva:
समाधानं किम् ?
चित्तैकाग्रता ।
units.translation: What is samādhāna? Steadiness of attention, with the mind gathered to one point.

units.label: Mumukṣutva — the desire for liberation
units.deva:
मुमुक्षुत्वं किम् ?
मोक्षो मे भूयाद् इति इच्छा ।
एतत् साधनचतुष्टयम् ।
ततस्तत्त्वविवेकस्याधिकारिणो भवन्ति ।
units.translation: What is the desire for liberation? The wish, “May liberation be mine.” These are the four preparations; through them students become qualified for inquiry into reality.

units.label: Inquiry into reality
units.deva:
तत्त्वविवेकः कः ?
आत्मा सत्यं तदन्यत् सर्वं मिथ्येति ।
units.translation: What is inquiry into reality? The Self is real; everything other than it is dependent appearance.

units.label: The Self — definition
units.deva:
आत्मा कः ?
स्थूलसूक्ष्मकारणशरीराद्व्यतिरिक्तः पञ्चकोशातीतः सन्
अवस्थात्रयसाक्षी सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपः सन्
यस्तिष्ठति स आत्मा ।
units.translation: What is the Self? That which remains distinct from the gross, subtle, and causal bodies; beyond the five sheaths; the witness of the three states; and of the nature of existence, awareness, and fullness — that is the Self.

gloss.en: from the gross, subtle, and causal bodies
of the nature of existence, awareness, and fullness

units.label: The gross body
units.deva:
स्थूलशरीरं किम् ?
पञ्चीकृतपञ्चमहाभूतैः कृतं सत्कर्मजन्यं
सुखदुःखादिभोगायतनं शरीरम् ।
अस्ति जायते वर्धते विपरिणमते अपक्षीयते विनश्यतीति
षड्विकारवदेतत्स्थूलशरीरम् ।
units.translation: What is the gross body? It is made from the five gross elements after their fivefold combination, arises from the results of past action, and serves as the dwelling in which pleasure, pain, and other experiences occur. It undergoes six changes: it exists, is born, grows, changes, declines, and perishes.

gloss.en: from the five gross elements mixed by fivefold combination

units.label: The subtle body
units.deva:
सूक्ष्मशरीरं किम् ?
अपञ्चीकृतपञ्चमहाभूतैः कृतं सत्कर्मजन्यं
सुखदुःखादिभोगसाधनं
पञ्चज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चकर्मेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चप्राणादयः
मनश्चैकं बुद्धिश्चैका
एवं सप्तदशकलाभिः सह यत्तिष्ठति तत्सूक्ष्मशरीरम् ।
units.translation: What is the subtle body? Made from the five elements before their gross combination and arising from past action, it is the instrument for experiences of pleasure, pain, and the like. It consists of the five organs of perception, five organs of action, five vital functions, the mind, and the intellect — seventeen constituents in all.

gloss.en: from the five elements before fivefold combination
the five vital functions and the rest

units.label: The organs of perception
units.deva:
श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुः रसना घ्राणम् इति पञ्च ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि ।
श्रोत्रस्य दिग्देवता । त्वचो वायुः । चक्षुषः सूर्यः ।
रसनाया वरुणः । घ्राणस्य अश्विनौ ।
इति ज्ञानेन्द्रियदेवताः ।
श्रोत्रस्य विषयः शब्दग्रहणम् । त्वचो विषयः स्पर्शग्रहणम् ।
चक्षुषो विषयः रूपग्रहणम् । रसनाया विषयः रसग्रहणम् ।
घ्राणस्य विषयः गन्धग्रहणम् इति ।
units.translation: The five organs of perception are hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell. Their presiding deities are, respectively, the deities of the directions, Vāyu, the Sun, Varuṇa, and the Aśvins. Their fields are, respectively, hearing sound, feeling contact, seeing form, tasting flavor, and perceiving scent.

units.label: The organs of action
units.deva:
वाक्पाणिपादपायूपस्थानीति पञ्चकर्मेन्द्रियाणि ।
वाचो देवता वह्निः । हस्तयोरिन्द्रः । पादयोर्विष्णुः ।
पायोर्मृत्युः । उपस्थस्य प्रजापतिः ।
इति कर्मेन्द्रियदेवताः ।
वाचो विषयः भाषणम् । पाण्योर्विषयः वस्तुग्रहणम् ।
पादयोर्विषयः गमनम् । पायोर्विषयः मलत्यागः ।
उपस्थस्य विषयः आनन्द इति ।
units.translation: The five organs of action are speech, the hands, the feet, the organ of excretion, and the generative organ. Their presiding deities are Fire, Indra, Viṣṇu, Death, and Prajāpati. Their functions are speaking, grasping objects, moving, elimination, and procreative pleasure.

units.label: The causal body
units.deva:
कारणशरीरं किम् ?
अनिर्वाच्यानाद्यविद्यारूपं शरीरद्वयस्य कारणमात्रं
सत्स्वरूपाऽज्ञानं निर्विकल्पकरूपं यदस्ति तत्कारणशरीरम् ।
units.translation: What is the causal body? It is beginningless ignorance, not describable as either real or unreal, the simple cause of the other two bodies, and a state in which distinctions have not yet unfolded.

units.label: The three states
units.deva:
अवस्थात्रयं किम् ?
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्त्यवस्थाः ।
units.translation: What are the three states? Waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.

units.label: Waking and dreaming
units.deva:
जाग्रदवस्था का ?
श्रोत्रादिज्ञानेन्द्रियैः शब्दादिविषयैश्च ज्ञायते इति यत्
सा जाग्रदवस्था । स्थूलशरीराभिमानी आत्मा विश्व इत्युच्यते ।
स्वप्नावस्था केति चेत् ? जाग्रदवस्थायां यद्दृष्टं यद् श्रुतम्
तज्जनितवासनया निद्रासमये यः प्रपञ्चः प्रतीयते सा
स्वप्नावस्था । सूक्ष्मशरीराभिमानी आत्मा तैजस इत्युच्यते ।
units.translation: What is the waking state? It is the state in which sound and other objects are known through the organs of perception, beginning with hearing. The Self identified with the gross body is called Viśva. What is the dream state? During sleep, the world that appears from impressions formed by what was seen and heard in waking is the dream state. The Self identified with the subtle body is called Taijasa.

gloss.en: through the organs of perception, beginning with hearing

units.label: Deep sleep
units.deva:
सुषुप्त्यवस्था का ?
अहं किमपि न जानामि सुखेन मया निद्रानुभूयत इति
सुषुप्त्यवस्था । कारणशरीराभिमानी आत्मा प्राज्ञ इत्युच्यते ।
units.translation: What is the state of deep sleep? It is the state later recalled as, “I knew nothing; I slept happily.” The Self identified with the causal body is called Prājña.

units.label: The five sheaths
units.deva:
पञ्च कोशाः के ?
अन्नमयः प्राणमयः मनोमयः विज्ञानमयः आनन्दमयश्चेति ।
units.translation: What are the five sheaths? The food sheath, vital-air sheath, mental sheath, intellect sheath, and bliss sheath.

units.label: The food sheath
units.deva:
अन्नमयः कः ?
अन्नरसेनैव भूत्वा अन्नरसेनैव वृद्धिं प्राप्य अन्नरूपपृथिव्यां
यद्विलीयते तदन्नमयः कोशः स्थूलशरीरम् ।
units.translation: What is the food sheath? That which is formed from the essence of food, grows through the essence of food, and dissolves back into the earth that becomes food: this is the food sheath, the gross body.

gloss.en: into the earth that takes the form of food

units.label: The vital-air sheath
units.deva:
प्राणमयः कः ?
प्राणाद्याः पञ्चवायवः वागादीन्द्रियपञ्चकं प्राणमयः कोशः ।
units.translation: What is the vital-air sheath? The five vital functions, beginning with prāṇa, together with the five organs of action, beginning with speech, constitute it.

gloss.en: the five organs of action beginning with speech

units.label: The mental sheath
units.deva:
मनोमयः कोशः कः ?
मनश्च ज्ञानेन्द्रियपञ्चकं मिलित्वा यो भवति स मनोमयः कोशः ।
units.translation: What is the mental sheath? That which consists of the mind together with the five organs of perception is the mental sheath.

units.label: The intellect sheath
units.deva:
विज्ञानमयः कः ?
बुद्धिज्ञानेन्द्रियपञ्चकं मिलित्वा यो भवति स विज्ञानमयः कोशः ।
units.translation: What is the intellect sheath? That which consists of the intellect together with the five organs of perception is the intellect sheath.

units.label: The bliss sheath and the five sheaths
units.deva:
आनन्दमयः कः ?
एवमेव कारणशरीरभूताविद्यास्थमलिनसत्त्वं
प्रियादिवृत्तिसहितं सत् आनन्दमयः कोशः ।
एतत्कोशपञ्चकम् ।
units.translation: What is the bliss sheath? It is the latent, clouded clarity abiding in ignorance, which is the causal body, together with mental states such as pleasure at the sight of what is dear. These are the five sheaths.

gloss.en: together with states such as pleasure at what is dear

units.label: The Self is distinct from the sheaths
units.deva:
मदीयं शरीरं मदीयाः प्राणाः मदीयं मनश्च
मदीया बुद्धिर्मदीयमज्ञानमिति स्वेनैव ज्ञायते ।
तद्यथा मदीयत्वेन ज्ञातं कटककुण्डलगृहादिकं
स्वस्माद्भिन्नं तथा पञ्चकोशादिकं स्वस्माद्भिन्नम् ।
मदीयत्वेन ज्ञातमात्मा न भवति ॥
units.translation: One knows directly, “My body, my vital functions, my mind, my intellect, my ignorance.” Just as a bracelet, an earring, a house, and the like, known as “mine,” are distinct from oneself, so too the five sheaths and related things are distinct from oneself. What is known as “mine” is not the Self.

gloss.en: bracelet, earring, house, and the like
the five sheaths and related things

units.label: The Self as existence, awareness, and fullness
units.deva:
आत्मा तर्हि कः ?
सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपः । सत्किम् ? कालत्रयेऽपि तिष्ठतीति सत् ।
चित्किम् ? ज्ञानस्वरूपः । आनन्दः कः ? सुखस्वरूपः ।
एवं सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपं स्वात्मानं विजानीयात् ।
units.translation: What, then, is the Self? It is of the nature of existence, awareness, and fullness. What is existence? That which remains in all three times is existence. What is awareness? The nature of knowing. What is fullness? The nature of happiness. Thus one should know one’s own Self as existence-awareness-fullness.

gloss.en: of the nature of existence, awareness, and fullness

units.label: Māyā and the twenty-four principles
units.deva:
अथ चतुर्विंशतितत्त्वोत्पत्तिप्रकारं वक्ष्यामः ।
ब्रह्माश्रया सत्त्वरजस्तमोगुणात्मिका माया अस्ति ।
units.translation: We now explain how the twenty-four principles arise. Māyā, supported by Brahman and constituted by the qualities sattva, rajas, and tamas, is present.

gloss.en: made of the qualities sattva, rajas, and tamas

units.label: The five elements
units.deva:
ततः आकाशः सम्भूतः । आकाशाद् वायुः । वायोस्तेजः ।
तेजस आपः । अद्भ्यः पृथिवी ।
units.translation: From it arose space; from space, air; from air, fire; from fire, water; and from water, earth.

units.label: Sattva and the sense organs
units.deva:
एतेषां पञ्चतत्त्वानां मध्ये
आकाशस्य सात्त्विकांशात् श्रोत्रेन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
वायोः सात्त्विकांशात् त्वगिन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
अग्नेः सात्त्विकांशात् चक्षुरिन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
जलस्य सात्त्विकांशात् रसनेन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
पृथिव्याः सात्त्विकांशात् घ्राणेन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
units.translation: From the sattva aspect of the five elements arose the organs of perception: hearing from space, touch from air, sight from fire, taste from water, and smell from earth.

gloss.en: from the sattva aspect of space

units.label: The inner instrument
units.deva:
एतेषां पञ्चतत्त्वानां समष्टिसात्त्विकांशात्
मनोबुद्ध्यहङ्कारचित्तान्तःकरणानि सम्भूतानि ।
सङ्कल्पविकल्पात्मकं मनः । निश्चयात्मिका बुद्धिः ।
अहङ्कर्ता अहङ्कारः । चिन्तनकर्तृ चित्तम् ।
मनसो देवता चन्द्रमाः । बुद्धे ब्रह्मा ।
अहङ्कारस्य रुद्रः । चित्तस्य वासुदेवः ।
units.translation: From the combined sattva aspect of the five elements arose the inner instrument in its four forms: mind, intellect, ego, and memory. The mind forms options and doubts; the intellect makes determinations; the ego is the sense of “I”; and the mind-stuff sustains recollection. Their presiding deities are the Moon, Brahmā, Rudra, and Vāsudeva, respectively.

units.label: Rajas and the organs of action
units.deva:
एतेषां पञ्चतत्त्वानां मध्ये
आकाशस्य राजसांशात् वागिन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
वायोः राजसांशात् पाणीन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
वह्नेः राजसांशात् पादेन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
जलस्य राजसांशात् उपस्थेन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
पृथिव्याः राजसांशात् गुदेन्द्रियं सम्भूतम् ।
एतेषां समष्टिराजसांशात् पञ्चप्राणाः सम्भूताः ।
units.translation: From the rajas aspect of the five elements arose the organs of action: speech from space, grasping from air, locomotion from fire, generation from water, and excretion from earth. From their combined rajas aspect arose the five vital functions.

units.label: Tamas and fivefold combination
units.deva:
एतेषां पञ्चतत्त्वानां तामसांशात्
पञ्चीकृतपञ्चतत्त्वानि भवन्ति ।
पञ्चीकरणं कथम् इति चेत् ।
एतेषां पञ्चमहाभूतानां तामसांशस्वरूपम्
एकमेकं भूतं द्विधा विभज्य एकमेकमर्धं पृथक्
तूष्णीं व्यवस्थाप्य अपरमपरमर्धं चतुर्धा विभज्य
स्वार्धमन्येष्वर्धेषु स्वभागचतुष्टयसंयोजनं कार्यम् ।
तदा पञ्चीकरणं भवति ।
units.translation: From the tamas aspect of these five elements arise the five gross elements through fivefold combination. How does this combination work? Divide each element into two halves. Set one half aside; divide the other half into four equal parts. Then combine the reserved half of each element with one quarter from each of the other four. This is fivefold combination.

gloss.en: the five elements mixed by fivefold combination
with the halves of the others

units.label: The body and the universe
units.deva:
एतेभ्यः पञ्चीकृतपञ्चमहाभूतेभ्यः स्थूलशरीरं भवति ।
एवं पिण्डब्रह्माण्डयोरैक्यं सम्भूतम् ।
units.translation: From these fivefold-combined elements comes the gross body. In this way, the individual body and the cosmic whole share the same elemental constitution.

gloss.en: from the five gross elements formed by fivefold combination
of the individual body and the universe

units.label: The individual and the Lord
units.deva:
स्थूलशरीराभिमानी जीवनामकं ब्रह्मप्रतिबिम्बं भवति ।
स एव जीवः प्रकृत्या स्वस्मादीश्वरं भिन्नत्वेन जानाति ।
अविद्योपाधिः सन्नात्मा जीव इत्युच्यते ।
मायोपाधिः सन्नीश्वर इत्युच्यते ।
एवमुपाधिभेदात् जीवेश्वरभेददृष्टिर्यावत्पर्यन्तं तिष्ठति
तावत्पर्यन्तं जन्ममरणादिरूपसंसारो न निवर्तते ।
तस्मात्कारणान्न जीवेश्वरयोर्भेदबुद्धिः स्वीकार्या ।
units.translation: The reflection of Brahman identified with the gross body is called the individual self, the jīva. By its nature it regards the Lord as separate from itself. Consciousness conditioned by ignorance is called the jīva; conditioned by Māyā, it is called Īśvara. As long as the apparent difference between jīva and Īśvara remains, saṃsāra — birth, death, and the rest — does not cease. Therefore their difference should not be taken as ultimate.

gloss.en: having the form of birth, death, and the rest
should not be accepted as final

units.label: “That thou art”
units.deva:
ननु साहङ्कारस्य किंचिज्ज्ञस्य जीवस्य निरहङ्कारस्य सर्वज्ञस्य
ईश्वरस्य तत्त्वमसीति महावाक्यात् कथमभेदबुद्धिः स्यात्
उभयोर्विरुद्धधर्माक्रान्तत्वात् । इति चेन्न ।
स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीराभिमानी त्वंपदवाच्यार्थः ।
उपाधिविनिर्मुक्तं समाधिदशासम्पन्नं शुद्धं चैतन्यं
त्वंपदलक्ष्यार्थः । एवं सर्वज्ञत्वादिविशिष्ट ईश्वरः
तत्पदवाच्यार्थः । उपाधिशून्यं शुद्धचैतन्यं तत्पदलक्ष्यार्थः ।
एवं च जीवेश्वरयोश्चैतन्यरूपेणाभेदे बाधकाभावः ।
units.translation: An objection arises: How can the great statement “That thou art” teach the identity of the jīva, which has ego and limited knowledge, with Īśvara, who is free of ego and all-knowing, since their attributes conflict? The answer is no. The direct meaning of “thou” is the one identified with the gross and subtle bodies; its implied meaning is pure consciousness, free from limiting conditions and realized in samādhi. The direct meaning of “that” is Īśvara endowed with omniscience and other attributes; its implied meaning is pure consciousness without limiting conditions. Thus nothing prevents the identity of the jīva and Īśvara in the nature of consciousness.

gloss.en: identified with gross and subtle bodies

units.label: The liberated person while living
units.deva:
एवं च वेदान्तवाक्यैः सद्गुरूपदेशेन च सर्वेष्वपि
भूतेषु येषां ब्रह्मबुद्धिरुत्पन्ना ते जीवन्मुक्ता इत्यर्थः ।
ननु जीवन्मुक्तः कः ? यथा देहोऽहं पुरुषोऽहं ब्राह्मणोऽहं
शूद्रोऽहमस्मीति दृढनिश्चयः तथा नाहं ब्राह्मणो न शूद्रो न पुरुषः
किन्त्वसङ्गः सच्चिदानन्दस्वरूपः प्रकाशरूपः सर्वान्तर्यामी
चिदाकाशरूपोऽस्मीति दृढनिश्चयरूपोऽपरोक्षज्ञानवान् जीवन्मुक्तः ॥
units.translation: Those in whom, through the statements of Vedānta and the instruction of a true teacher, the understanding of Brahman has arisen with regard to all beings are liberated while living. Who is such a person? Just as one may be firmly convinced, “I am the body, a man, a brāhmaṇa, a śūdra,” the liberated person has the direct and firm knowledge: “I am not a brāhmaṇa, a śūdra, or a man; I am unattached, of the nature of existence-awareness-fullness, self-luminous, the indweller of all, and boundless consciousness.”

gloss.en: of the nature of existence, awareness, and fullness
of the nature of boundless consciousness

units.label: The three kinds of action
units.deva:
ब्रह्मैवाहमस्मीत्यपरोक्षज्ञानेन निखिलकर्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्तः स्यात् ।
कर्माणि कतिविधानीति चेत् आगामिसञ्चितप्रारब्धभेदेन
त्रिविधानि सन्ति ।
ज्ञानोत्पत्त्यनन्तरं ज्ञानिदेहकृतं पुण्यपापरूपं कर्म
यदस्ति तदागामीत्यभिधीयते ।
सञ्चितं कर्म किम् ? अनन्तकोटिजन्मनां बीजभूतं सत्
यत्कर्मजातं पूर्वार्जितं तिष्ठति तत्सञ्चितं ज्ञेयम् ।
प्रारब्धं कर्म किम् ? इदं शरीरमुत्पाद्य इह लोके सुखदुःखादिप्रदं
यत्कर्म तत्प्रारब्धम् । भोगेन नष्टं भवति ।
units.translation: Through the direct knowledge “I alone am Brahman,” one becomes free from the bondage of all action. How many kinds of action are there? Three: āgāmi, sañcita, and prārabdha. Action, whether meritorious or harmful, performed by the body of a knower after knowledge has arisen is called āgāmi. What is sañcita action? It is the accumulated action already performed, remaining as the seed of countless future births. What is prārabdha action? It is the action that has produced this body and gives experiences of pleasure, pain, and the like in this life; it is exhausted through experience.

gloss.en: performed by the body of a knower
in the form of merit or demerit

units.label: Freedom from action and the fruit of knowledge
units.deva:
सञ्चितं कर्म ब्रह्मैवाहमिति निश्चयात्मकज्ञानेन नश्यति ।
आगामि कर्मापि ज्ञानेन नश्यति ।
किञ्चागामिकर्मणां नलिनीदलगतजलवज्ज्ञानिनां सम्बन्धो नास्ति ।
ये ज्ञानिनं स्तुवन्ति भजन्त्यर्चयन्ति तान्प्रति ज्ञानिकृतमागामि पुण्यं गच्छति ।
ये ज्ञानिनं निन्दन्ति द्विषन्ति दुःखप्रदानं कुर्वन्ति तान्प्रति
ज्ञानिकृतं सर्वमागामि क्रियमाणं यदवाच्यं कर्म पापात्मकं तद्गच्छति ।
सुहृदः पुण्यकृतं दुर्हृदः पापकृत्यं गृह्णन्ति ।
तथा चात्मवित्संसारं तीर्त्वा ब्रह्मानन्दमिहैव प्राप्नोति ।
तरति शोकमात्मवित् इति श्रुतेः ।
units.translation: Accumulated action is destroyed by the firm knowledge “I am Brahman”; future action is also destroyed by knowledge. Future action does not cling to a knower, just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf. The merit arising from the knower’s future actions goes to those who praise, serve, and honor the knower; the harmful results go to those who condemn, hate, or injure the knower. Well-wishers receive the merit, and ill-wishers the harmful results. Thus the knower of the Self crosses saṃsāra and attains the bliss of Brahman here itself, as the Upaniṣad says: “The knower of the Self crosses sorrow.”

gloss.en: like water on a lotus leaf

units.label: Final teaching and colophon
units.deva:
तनुं त्यजतु वा काश्यां श्वपचस्य गृहेऽथ वा ।
ज्ञानसम्प्राप्तिसमये मुक्तोऽसौ विगताशयः ॥ इति स्मृतेश्च ।
इति श्रीशङ्करभगवत्पादाचार्यप्रणीतं तत्त्वबोधप्रकरणं समाप्तम् ॥
units.translation: Whether the body falls away in Kāśī or in the home of an outcaste, at the very moment knowledge is attained the person is free, with all latent tendencies exhausted — so says the Smṛti. Thus ends the treatise Tattvabodha, attributed in its closing colophon to the revered Śaṅkara Bhagavatpādācārya.

gloss.en: in the home of an outcaste
at the moment knowledge is attained
attributed as composed by the revered Śaṅkara Bhagavatpādācārya
